changes.after: A method is a named set of instructions you can call with an input.

before: A method is a named group of Ruby instructions. def starts a method definition and end finishes it.
def double_score(n) creates a parameter named n. Calling double_score(4) supplies the argument 4.
Ruby returns the last evaluated expression from a method when no explicit return is used. Here n * 2 provides that result.
Defining the method is not calling it. puts displays the result of the call, and each call can supply a different argument.

```ruby
def double_score(n)
  n * 2
end
puts double_score(4)
```
Expected result: 8. Follow the instructions in order; this is a worked example, not an in-app execution.
after: A method is a named set of instructions you can call with an input.
The number in the call takes the local name n.
Ruby uses the last expression in this method as its answer.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
def double_score(n)
  n * 2
end
puts double_score(4)
```
The output is `8`. The call supplies four. Twice four is eight.
